# Product Feedback Coordinator

This skill prepares a product owner decision from current, authorized feedback and product records. It does not authorize a roadmap or issue-tracker change.

## Setup in chat

Read templates/product-feedback-coordinator/TEMPLATE_SETUP.json and templates/product-feedback-coordinator/SETUP.md. Verify each check on real authorized records before adding its ID to completed_steps. Preserve existing Crew identity and setup progress. Report verified, blocked and next.

## First useful result

1. Bind exact tenant, product, theme, period, affected segment, owner and feedback source scope.
2. Inspect the validated theme and its deduplicated source IDs, denominator, coverage and counterexamples. Separate reported pain from an observed product defect.
3. Re-read current issue, roadmap, release and product-usage records. Match an existing issue by exact problem and scope; flag weak or ambiguous matches.
4. Compare owner criteria: severity, reach, segment, strategic relevance, evidence quality, effort unknowns and existing commitments. A count alone is not a priority score.
5. Present options: investigate, link to an existing item, prepare a new candidate, decline, or defer. Record the product owner decision and evidence needed next.

Deliver **A product decision brief with theme and feedback IDs, affected scope, existing issue links, evidence gaps, owner decision options and next verification.** Every factual claim needs feedback or product source IDs, observed time, coverage and an owner decision state.

## Fictional worked example

Fictional input: theme F-9 reports confusing invite permissions from 9 of 40 surveyed respondents plus 3 linked cases, all from one segment. Current tracker issue ISSUE-18 concerns a different admin permission error; roadmap has no committed invite change.

Fictional output: decision brief P-9 binds F-9 and its 40-response denominator; affected segment=one onboarding cohort; ISSUE-18 is related but not an exact duplicate; observed usage impact=unknown; recommendation=investigate invite copy with Product and Support; owner decision=pending; new issue=none; customer promise=none.

Inadequate: “Everyone has this bug. ISSUE-18 fixes it; promise customers the change next week.” Reason: prevalence, issue identity and delivery date are unsupported, and no product owner approved a commitment.

## Later run

Re-read current issue, roadmap and product evidence; retain theme and issue IDs, preserve accepted and declined decisions, and report what changed instead of opening duplicate work.

## Boundaries

Do not promise a feature, rank a roadmap by mention count alone, create or close an issue, change priority, publish a plan, or message a customer without owner approval and a separate route. Installation enables no schedule, trigger, function, Automation, issue write or customer message.

# Product Feedback Coordinator setup

Template product-feedback-coordinator version 1. Progress lives in templates/product-feedback-coordinator/TEMPLATE_SETUP.json and is verified through Crew chat.

## First result

Provide Validated feedback theme or authorized feedback records, product and account scope, current issue or roadmap source, product owner and decision criteria. Ask: “Review this onboarding feedback theme against current product issues and propose the next owner decision.”

Expected: **A product decision brief with theme and feedback IDs, affected scope, existing issue links, evidence gaps, owner decision options and next verification.** Cite feedback scope, denominator, representative and contrary cases, existing issue state, and owner decision.

## Sources and boundaries

Helpdesk/survey exports, product usage records, issue tracker and roadmap through scoped MCPs or files. A read-only first decision uses authorized exports. Start with one authorized theme and current issue/roadmap read. Do not promise a feature, rank a roadmap by mention count alone, create or close an issue, change priority, publish a plan, or message a customer without owner approval and a separate route.

## Repeat policy

Re-read current issue, roadmap and product evidence; retain theme and issue IDs, preserve accepted and declined decisions, and report what changed instead of opening duplicate work. Builder must test one real case and the owner must review any action or recurrence before activation.
